children.translated_text: O Blessed One, Lord of the gods of gods,
Lord of the worlds, Master of the universe!
The <s>mantra-tantra</s> (science of mantras and rituals) has been taught by you
in detail, as a means of accomplishing [all] purposes.
These mortals are of short life,
of little strength and little intellect,
of little courage and little wealth,
possessed of greed and delusion.
A text that is brief yet of great meaning,
abounding in a multitude of topics —
please speak, O God, for their
benefit, O my Lord!
Now then, I shall teach
this <s>śāstra</s> (scripture), supremely rare,
extracted from the <s>tantra</s> called <s>Vātula</s>,
like clarified butter from curds.
That supreme seed called <s>nāda</s> (primordial sound),
which abides in all beings,
which grants liberation, supreme, and moreover
bestows divine <s>siddhis</s> (supernatural accomplishments) —
having known that, O <s>Mahāsena</s> (Skanda),
one becomes a <s>deśika</s> (teacher) who destroys bonds.
Even cowherds, women, children,
<s>mlecchas</s> (barbarians), and speakers of common language —
even creatures dwelling within water —
they too constantly utter it.
Knowing the gross, subtle, and supreme,
one should perform actions as desired.
The gross is declared to be sound (<s>śabda</s>);
the subtle consists of thought (<s>cintā</s>);
that which is free from thought —
that is proclaimed as the supreme.
Ending in <s>anusvāra</s>, all-pervading, void,
established in the group of twelve <s>mātrās</s> (measures).
The <s>Brahmāṇi</s> (seed syllables of Brahmā) are declared to be the short [vowels];
the long [vowels] are the <s>aṅgas</s> (ancillary mantras), O <s>Ṣaṇmukha</s> (Six-faced one).
<s>Anusvāra</s> becomes the <s>netra</s> (eye-weapon mantra),
stationed above all of them.
With <s>visarga</s>, it becomes the <s>astra</s> (weapon-mantra),
without <s>anusvāra</s>.
The sixth [vowel] up to the thirteenth
should be applied to the fifth.
One should know that as <s>Śiva</s> —
the <s>mantra</s>-form, <s>Sadāśiva</s>.
The second of its sixth,
combined with the initial of the fourth [group],
from the second and the fifth,
one should join the first again.
It destroys obstacles with the <s>Śivāstra</s> (weapon of Śiva);
with the <s>śikhā</s> (topknot mantra), it is remembered as granting liberation.
This is the divine <s>Pāśupata</s>,
which cuts all bonds.
The <s>Brahmāṇi</s> [mantras] and <s>Śiva</s> with his <s>aṅgas</s> (ancillaries),
the <s>netra</s> and the <s>Pāśupata</s> —
in brief, all this auspicious
<s>mantroddhāra</s> (extraction of mantras) has been stated.
I shall now teach the <s>mudrā</s> (ritual gesture) of this,
for the benefit of <s>sādhakas</s> (practitioners).
With both hands, one should touch from the feet
upward to the crown of the head.
This <s>mudrā</s> is the <s>mahāmudrā</s> (great gesture),
which accomplishes all desires and purposes.
Having first performed the <s>karanyāsa</s> (hand-placement),
one should then form the <s>mudrābandha</s> (gesture-seal).
The palm and the back of the hand
should be purified with the <s>astra-bīja</s> (weapon seed-syllable).
Beginning with the little finger
and the thumb last,
one should place the <s>Brahmāṇi</s> [mantras] there,
and likewise the <s>aṅgas</s> (ancillary mantras) carefully.
Afterwards, one should place the <s>Prāsāda</s> [mantra],
pervading and facing all directions.
First chapter.
The placement of the inner worship (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>),
and likewise the purification of the elements (<s>bhūtaśuddhi</s>).
Having first performed <s>bhūtaśuddhi</s> (elemental purification),
then perform the inner worship (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>).
The <s>hṛdbīja</s> (heart seed-syllable) joined with the earth [element] —
one should perform the earth <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration) in sequence.
The head in water, the <s>śikhā</s> (topknot) in fire,
the <s>kavaca</s> (armor) together with wind,
and the <s>astra</s> (weapon) joined with <s>Śiva</s> —
one should always perform the space <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration).
Piercing the veil with the ending '<s>huṃ phaṭ</s>,'
one rises upward especially.
Five upward thrusts (<s>udghātas</s>), four,
three, two, and one.
At the end of the twelve [finger-breadths above], unsupported,
pure consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>) alone abides.
As in <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation), O child,
so one should perform that practice.
One should then contemplate the <s>amṛta</s> (nectar)
at the end of the procedure, flowing [downward].
With <s>Oṃ</s>, the lotus
then becomes the <s>yogapīṭha</s> (seat of yoga).
Resembling the solar disc,
the letter '<s>a</s>' is born of the self (<s>ātman</s>).
The <s>vidyā-tattva</s> (knowledge principle) is the letter '<s>u</s>';
the <s>Śiva-tattva</s> (Śiva principle) is born of the letter '<s>m</s>'.
The <s>puryaṣṭaka</s> (subtle body) and <s>tanmātra</s> (subtle elements),
<s>turyātīta</s> (beyond the fourth state) is <s>Sadāśiva</s>.
One should contemplate the supreme abode,
piercing the crown through the <s>suṣumnā</s> (central channel).
One should visualize oneself as pervaded by that,
completely filled.
The mortal who would practice such
<s>samādhi</s> (absorption) that destroys death —
for him, death does not arise;
this is the firm determination of the <s>śāstra</s> (scripture).
Afterwards, for the <s>guru</s> (teacher) and the <s>sādhakas</s> (practitioners),
the assumption of forms takes place.
Beginning with <s>Īśāna</s> and ending with <s>Sadyojāta</s>,
one should place [the mantras] starting from the crown.
Having given the <s>netra</s> (eye mantra), then one should invoke
the God of gods, <s>Sadāśiva</s>.
The wise one should then contemplate himself
as omniscient.
The <s>hṛdaya</s> (heart), the <s>śiras</s> (head),
the <s>śikhā</s> (topknot), and the <s>kavaca</s> (armor) —
the knower of <s>mantras</s> should place the <s>astra</s> (weapon)
at their respective stations in order.
In the heart, one should arrange the worship (<s>arcā</s>);
at the navel, one should perform the <s>homa</s> (fire oblation).
On the forehead, one should meditate on <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord),
the boon-giver, facing all directions.
As in worship (<s>arcana</s>), so in the fire [ritual],
in meditation, and in bathing likewise.
As in the deity (<s>deva</s>), so in the body —
the wise one should contemplate.
Having thus performed the inner worship (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>),
afterwards the external [worship], O <s>Ṣaṇmukha</s> (Six-faced one).
Having performed both the external and internal [worship],
one should then commence the ritual worship (<s>yajana</s>).
Chapter on the placement of the inner worship (<s>antaḥkaraṇavinyāsa</s>) — thus the second chapter.
Hereafter I shall teach
the bathing (<s>snāna</s>) that removes sin, auspicious.
Having recited once and taken up
earth with the <s>astra</s> [mantra], the knower of <s>mantras</s>
should first perform the impurity-removing bath (<s>malasnāna</s>),
and having recited the <s>saṃhitā</s> once,
should then consecrate that very clay
by reciting over it once each time.
Then, having divided it into three parts,
one should consecrate one part with the <s>astra</s> [mantra],
the second with the <s>Brahma</s> [mantras], O child,
and the third recited with the <s>Śiva</s> [mantra].
With the part consecrated by the <s>astra</s>,
one should perform the sealing of the directions (<s>digbandhana</s>).
With the part consecrated by <s>Śiva</s>, one creates the <s>tīrtha</s> (sacred water);
with the part consecrated by <s>Brahma</s>, [one consecrates] the body.
Having paralyzed [impurities], one should then bathe
in the midst of the <s>Śivatīrtha</s> (sacred waters of Śiva),
with the <s>cakravat</s> procedure (circular method),
with fragrant <s>āmalaka</s> (Indian gooseberry) and the like.
Having sipped water according to the prescribed method,
the <s>sādhaka</s> (practitioner) should salute the twilight (<s>sandhyā</s>).
With all <s>mantras</s>, reciting once, O child,
one should perform the <s>upasthāna</s> (approach [to the deity]).
Having first performed the <s>abhiṣeka</s> (consecration bath),
one should then perform the <s>sandhyā</s> (twilight worship).
One should not apply the <s>astra</s> [mantra] to the body;
one should cast it outward only.
It would dry up the body, O child;
therefore one should not apply it to oneself.
Against obstacles and webs of bondage,
the wise should always employ it.
Then, the learned one, with the <s>hṛdaya</s> (heart mantra),
should offer <s>tarpaṇa</s> (libations) to the ancestors and gods.
The dissolution of that <s>tīrtha</s> (sacred water)
should be performed with the <s>Prāsāda</s> [mantra] alone.
Chapter on water-bathing (<s>vāruṇasnāna</s>) — thus the third chapter.
I shall teach the ash-bathing (<s>bhasmasnāna</s>)
and what follows it, O <s>Ṣaḍānana</s> (Six-faced one).
With all <s>mantras</s>, one should consecrate the ashes
once, in the proper order.
Having first performed the water-bath,
with the <s>astra-bīja</s> (weapon seed-syllable), O <s>Ṣaṇmukha</s>,
one should then perform the prescribed bath (<s>vidhisnāna</s>),
the knower of <s>mantras</s>, beginning from the crown.
One should bathe the head with <s>Īśāna</s>,
the face with <s>Tatpuruṣa</s>,
the heart with <s>Bahurūpa</s> (<s>Aghora</s>),
the secret parts with <s>Guhyaka</s> (<s>Vāmadeva</s>).
All limbs with <s>Ajāta</s> (<s>Sadyojāta</s>);
the <s>abhiṣeka</s> (sprinkling consecration) with the five [Brahmā mantras].
From above, with the <s>Prāsāda</s> [mantra],
one should perform the bath, O <s>Ṣaṇmukha</s>.
Chapter on ash-bathing (<s>bhasmasnāna</s>) — thus the fourth chapter.
I shall teach the worship (<s>yajana</s>)
in proper order according to the rules.
First the seed-sprout (<s>bījāṅkura</s>) with <s>Śakti</s> (power),
then the seat of <s>Ananta</s>.
One should make <s>Ananta</s> the base,
in sequence, O <s>Ṣaḍānana</s>.
The <s>hṛdaya</s> (heart) is the pericarp; the lotus [is the seat];
<s>Dharma</s> (righteousness), <s>Jñāna</s> (knowledge), and the rest,
<s>Vairāgya</s> (detachment) and <s>Aiśvarya</s> (sovereignty) —
ending with <s>Īśāna</s>, one should place them starting from the fire [direction].
The array of filaments with the <s>Śaktis</s> (powers),
one should fashion with the <s>hṛdaya</s> (heart mantra).
Then one should invoke the deity
with the <s>hṛdaya</s> (heart mantra), O <s>Ṣaṇmukha</s>.
Establishing, <s>pādya</s> (foot-washing water), <s>arghya</s> (offering water),
and likewise <s>ācamana</s> (sipping water),
bathing and worship —
one should perform with the <s>hṛdaya</s> (heart mantra).
Whatever has been mentioned or not mentioned,
all of that should be done with the <s>hṛdaya</s> (heart mantra).
This is the single-enclosure [worship],
which accomplishes all desires and purposes.
It is common to all <s>tantras</s>,
and supreme among all [forms of] knowledge.
Chapter on worship (<s>yajana</s>) — thus the fifth chapter.
Hereafter I shall teach
the procedure for fire rites (<s>agnikārya</s>) in order.
With the <s>astra</s> [mantra], one should perform the tracing [of lines],
then the sprinkling with the <s>varman</s> (armor mantra).
The placement of <s>Śakti</s> (power) then, with <s>darbha</s> grasses,
should be performed with the <s>hṛdaya</s> (heart mantra) alone.
With the heart [mantra], into the womb of <s>Śakti</s>,
one should cast the fire (<s>Jātavedas</s>).
Having performed the <s>garbhādhāna</s> (conception rite) and the rest,
and the <s>niṣkṛti</s> (expiation) at the end,
the knower of <s>mantras</s>, with the <s>hṛdaya</s> (heart mantra) alone,
should perform all rites.
Afterwards, the lotus arrangement
described earlier should be set up.
All <s>mantras</s> beginning with <s>Śiva</s>
should be offered into the fire in order.
Chapter on fire rites (<s>agnikārya</s>) — thus the sixth chapter.
Hereafter I shall teach
the <s>maṇḍala</s> (ritual diagram) that fulfills all desires.
Having purified the ground
by the rite prescribed in the <s>śāstra</s>,
then having performed the <s>adhivāsa</s> (consecration eve),
under a <s>nakṣatra</s> (constellation) associated with the <s>guru</s> (Jupiter),
the wise one should draw the <s>maṇḍala</s> (ritual diagram),
auspicious, bestowing all <s>siddhis</s> (accomplishments).
Having made it well-measured with a cord,
square on all sides,
in the center, a lotus should be established
with eight petals and a pericarp.
One <s>hasta</s> (cubit), two <s>hastas</s>,
or even four <s>hastas</s> —
the wise one, as prescribed in the [relevant] <s>tantra</s>,
should draw three enclosures.
The <s>ācārya</s> (preceptor), well-concentrated,
should open the western door.
In the southeastern direction, one should construct the <s>kuṇḍa</s> (fire-pit),
of one <s>hasta</s> (cubit) in measure.
One should perform the rite of sacrificial fire
in the well-kindled fire.
Beginning from the east, one should place the faces [of Śiva]
and the rest in order.
Having first placed the <s>pavitras</s> (purificatory items),
one should then place the <s>Śivāṅgas</s> (limb-mantras of Śiva).
In the southeastern direction, one should place the <s>hṛdaya</s> (heart);
in the northeastern direction, the <s>śiras</s> (head).
In the southwestern direction, the <s>śikhā</s> (topknot) is to be known;
the <s>kavaca</s> (armor) in the domain of wind (northwest).
Having placed the <s>astra</s> (weapon) in the [intermediate] directions,
and <s>Sadāśiva</s> in the pericarp,
the procedure for the inner placement (<s>garbhanyāsa</s>) has been declared.
Hear about the second enclosure.
Beginning from the east, with the <s>hṛdaya</s> (heart mantra),
one should worship the <s>lokapālas</s> (world-guardians).
In the third enclosure, one should worship the <s>astras</s> (weapons) with their own <s>mantras</s>.
In brief, O <s>Skanda</s>,
the procedure has been described by me.
Whatever has not been mentioned,
all of that should resort to the root [text].
Thus, the one who knows the rules and procedures
should perform the rite of <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation).
Chapter on the procedure for <s>maṇḍala</s> construction — thus the seventh chapter.
Now I shall teach the <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation),
established upon the five <s>tattvas</s> (principles).
Earth, water, fire,
wind, and space —
these are the five <s>tattvas</s> (principles)
by which the entire universe is pervaded.
All <s>tattvas</s> should be seen
within these very [five] by the <s>sādhakas</s> (practitioners).
In the cosmic egg (<s>brahmāṇḍa</s>), <s>Nivṛtti</s> (cessation) indeed [is the first <s>kalā</s>],
extending up to the hundred <s>Rudras</s>.
Above that is <s>Pratiṣṭhā</s> (establishment),
extending to the domain of the Unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>).
Then <s>Vidyā</s> (knowledge) is assigned,
extending to the vicinity of <s>Vidyeśvara</s> (Lord of Knowledge).
<s>Śānti</s> (peace) is above that, at the end of the cosmic path (<s>adhvan</s>);
<s>Śakti</s> (power) indeed is in the station of <s>Śiva</s>.
One who wishes to perform <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation)
without knowing these <s>tattvas</s> (principles) —
his effort is in vain;
he shall never obtain its fruit.
<s>Nivṛtti</s> (cessation) is to be known as earth;
<s>Pratiṣṭhā</s> (establishment) is called water.
One should know <s>Vidyā</s> (knowledge) as fire;
wind is declared as <s>Śānti</s> (peace).
<s>Śāntyatītā</s> (that which transcends peace) is space;
beyond that is the tranquil, imperishable [Śiva].
Having known that, O <s>Mahāsena</s>,
one may initiate even a <s>śvapaca</s> (outcaste).
The <s>guru</s> should offer <s>Nivṛtti</s> with the <s>hṛdaya</s> (heart mantra) alone,
<s>Pratiṣṭhā</s> with the <s>śiras</s> (head mantra);
<s>Śiva</s> [should offer] <s>Vidyā</s> with the <s>śikhā</s> (topknot mantra),
<s>Śānti</s> with the <s>kavaca</s> (armor mantra).
<s>Śāntyatītā</s>, the supreme space —
one should offer into the fire with the <s>Prāsāda</s> [mantra].
One hundred oblations for each [kalā]
should be offered — thus five oblations [sets].
Five complete oblations (<s>pūrṇāhutis</s>) should be given
with the <s>Prāsāda</s> [mantra], O <s>Ṣaṇmukha</s>.
For the purpose of purification through expiation (<s>prāyaścitta</s>),
eight oblations for each [kalā].
The knower of <s>mantras</s>, with the <s>astra-bīja</s> (weapon seed-syllable),
should offer oblations in order.
Thus the <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation) is completed,
free from [the need for further] birth and the like.
By the fire oblation alone, <s>sādhakas</s> (practitioners) are freed
from the bondage of birth.
This <s>iṣṭi</s> (sacrifice) should not be made public;
it should be guarded with effort.
It is the secret of all <s>tantras</s>;
this is the supreme <s>saṃskāra</s> (consecration).
The rite of placing the <s>yoni</s> (womb, cosmic matrix) and the rest,
and the extraction (<s>uddhāraṇa</s>), which comes last —
O God, please describe the order of purification
according to the proper procedure.
The ten and seven that are to be purified,
about which you have been asked, O <s>Guha</s> (Skanda),
the seed of each that has been stated —
I shall teach that in order.
The <s>yoni-bīja</s> (womb seed-syllable) in the heart —
one should set up in proper order.
Worship (<s>arcana</s>), sprinkling (<s>prokṣaṇa</s>),
and then striking (<s>tāḍana</s>), the supreme,
joining (<s>saṃdhāna</s>) and union (<s>saṃyoga</s>),
deposition (<s>nikṣepa</s>) thereafter,
and then worship (<s>arcana</s>) should be performed,
and likewise the conception rite (<s>garbhādhāna</s>),
birth (<s>janana</s>), empowerment (<s>adhikāra</s>),
enjoyment (<s>bhoga</s>), and dissolution (<s>laya</s>) likewise.
In each <s>tattva</s> (principle), one hundred oblations
with the <s>hṛdaya</s> (heart mantra), O <s>Ṣaṇmukha</s>.
The cutting of bonds (<s>pāśaccheda</s>) then with the <s>astra</s> [mantra];
one should give the complete oblation (<s>pūrṇāhuti</s>) thereafter.
The extraction (<s>uddhāra</s>) here with the <s>hṛdaya</s> (heart mantra)
should be performed in proper order.
In the extraction, the sprinkling,
and the striking likewise,
joined with the sounds '<s>huṃ phaṭ</s>' —
it should be done in proper order.
And the joining (<s>saṃdhāna</s>) of the <s>tattvas</s> (principles)
should be performed in the proper sequence.
In each <s>tattva</s> (principle), this ritual action [should be performed];
this indeed is the prescribed sequence.
By these purified [principles], O child,
one attains the complete rite.
Otherwise they are never liberated,
those who lack the [proper] rite, O <s>Ṣaḍānana</s> (Six-faced One).
And the offering of the final oblation (<s>pūrṇāhuti</s>)
should be performed accompanied by <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration).
That which is the supreme nectar (<s>amṛta</s>), O child,
one should visualize it flowing, with the mind.
In the section on <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation), this indeed
should be applied everywhere, at all times.
And in the procedure of <s>liṅgoddhāra</s> (extraction of the liṅga),
in the daily consecration rites —
as for the seizing and releasing of the bound soul (<s>paśu</s>)
that you spoke of earlier, O sinless one —
the bonds (<s>pāśas</s>), inner and outer,
in what place are they situated?
And in what place should they be severed?
How does the immediate ascent (<s>utkramaṇa</s>) [of the soul take place]?
Describe to me also the specification
of the bound souls (<s>paśus</s>), O <s>Maheśvara</s> (Great Lord).
Of the first [soul], having grasped the self by the self
with the second [finger],
with the fist, the skilled one should lead him
to that station.
Through the conjunction of the equinox (<s>viṣuvat</s>),
those from <s>Brahmā</s> to <s>Śiva</s>
attain unity in one [place];
otherwise, [they remain] separately.
At the <s>dvādaśānta</s> (the end of twelve [finger-breadths above the head]) they should be severed,
conjoined with the arrow and the weapon (<s>astra</s>).
Then they attain <s>sāyujya</s> (union [with Śiva]),
freed from the observances (<s>samayas</s>).
That which is performed without designation and without naming
becomes futile.
The ritual action performed with him as the object
bestows liberation — there is no doubt.
At the eclipse of the sun, O child,
conjoined with the equinox conjunction (<s>viṣuvadyoga</s>),
when [the breath] is cut at the end of the extension (<s>āyāma</s>),
then the ascent (<s>utkramaṇa</s>) certainly occurs.
The bonds (<s>pāśas</s>) are strung upon the mind
like clusters of gems upon a thread.
From the lotus of the heart (<s>hṛtpadma</s>) up to that [uppermost] lotus,
the thread of the mind is extended.
Having seen that, one should perform the cutting
with the mind-cutter, through the activity of the mind.
When the mind is cut by the mind within the mind,
the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) attains the state of isolation (<s>kevalatā</s>).
Leave aside the elaborate [account], O Lord of the Gods;
tell me in brief
that by which, merely by being known,
one liberates the bound souls (<s>paśus</s>) in an instant.
Listen, O <s>Ṣaṇmukha</s> (Six-faced One), to the true principle
by which liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>) certainly comes about.
Through an exceedingly subtle application,
the knower of <s>mantras</s>, perceiving through <s>yoga</s>,
through the divine path of <s>yoga</s>,
should impel that <s>śakti</s> (power).
Having known that, O <s>Mahāsena</s>,
the wise one [should know] the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) as constituted of <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath),
and through the conjunction of the equinox (<s>viṣuvat</s>),
should unite [it] with the eternal station.
Having attained the equinox conjunction (<s>viṣuva</s>) in <s>yoga</s>,
who would not be released from bondage?
The <s>nāḍīs</s> (channels) [associated with] the lotuses of earth and the other [elements],
with the winds possessing the qualities of sound and the rest,
the self, the presiding deities, and the <s>mantras</s> —
having known [these], the liberated one should liberate [others].
Connected with the openings of the <s>nāḍīs</s> (channels),
with upward stems and downward-facing [openings],
all [the channels] are endowed with two knots,
conjoined with [the syllables ending in] <s>HUṂ PHAṬ</s>.
Then they attain the upward [state]
through the <s>udghātas</s> (percussions) as before, O <s>Guha</s> (the Hidden One).
Having contemplated with the mind the [principles] beginning with earth,
again, both externally and internally,
in each <s>tattva</s> (principle), [the elements] should be directed,
separated and free from ego-sense.
One should cause [the beings] from <s>Brahmā</s> onward to hear, O child,
[so that they] do not go to the state of rebirth.
Having practiced the fire and consciousness twice,
the extension (<s>āyāma</s>) is [that] of the sun.
Having struck first, O child,
the seizing should be as before.
Having broken open the bolt, one should deposit [the soul] in the <s>yoni</s> (source);
one should join <s>tattva</s> (principle) with <s>tattva</s>,
having enclosed [them] with the <s>śaktis</s> (powers),
one should deposit [them] with [the syllable ending in] <s>VAUṢAṬ</s>.
Section on <s>Dīkṣā</s> (Initiation) — the eighth chapter.
I shall now teach the <s>abhiṣeka</s> (consecration)
in brief, not in detail,
for the benefit of the foremost <s>sādhakas</s> (practitioners),
as spoken by <s>Parameśa</s> (the Supreme Lord).
A single earthen vessel (<s>kalaśa</s>),
anointed with sandalwood paste,
or a cup of <s>Brahmā</s>-leaves,
or else of lotus petals —
having prepared it with all medicinal herbs
and adorned with all fragrances,
having recited [the mantra] one hundred and eight times
over the temple (<s>prāsāda</s>) facing all directions,
having performed the worship (<s>yāga</s>) as previously described,
one should perform the <s>abhiṣeka</s> (consecration),
on a day with an auspicious <s>nakṣatra</s> (lunar mansion),
at a <s>muhūrta</s> (auspicious moment) endowed with [proper] <s>karaṇa</s> (half-lunar-day).
With the resounding of many auspicious [instruments],
with the sounds of conch-shells and musical instruments,
with various Vedic recitations (<s>brahmaghoṣa</s>),
accompanied by dance and song —
having been authorized and consecrated,
the <s>ācārya</s> (preceptor) becomes a destroyer of bonds (<s>pāśahā</s>).
Section on <s>Abhiṣeka</s> (Consecration) — the ninth chapter.
I shall teach the supreme, subtle <s>nāḍīcakra</s> (wheel of channels)
in proper sequence.
Below the navel, there is a bulb (<s>kanda</s>),
from which sprouts emerge.
Seventy-two thousand [<s>nāḍīs</s>]
are established in the center of the navel.
Sideways, upwards, and downwards,
they pervade [the body] from the navel in all directions.
The <s>nāḍīs</s> (channels) are arranged like a wheel;
among them, those that are principal are ten.
<s>Iḍā</s> and <s>Piṅgalā</s>,
and <s>Suṣumnā</s> as the third,
<s>Gāndhārī</s> and <s>Hastijihvā</s>,
<s>Pūṣā</s> and <s>Yaśā</s> likewise,
<s>Alambuṣā</s> and <s>Kuhū</s>,
and <s>Śaṅkhinī</s> is known as the tenth.
These ten <s>nāḍīs</s> (channels) are declared
to be the carriers of <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath).
<s>Prāṇa</s>, <s>Apāna</s>, <s>Samāna</s>,
<s>Udāna</s>, and <s>Vyāna</s> indeed,
<s>Nāga</s>, <s>Kūrma</s>, then <s>Kṛkara</s>,
<s>Devadatta</s>, and <s>Dhanañjaya</s> —
<s>Prāṇa</s> is the foremost wind;
he is the lord of the [other] nine as well.
<s>Prāṇa</s>, constituted of <s>prāṇa</s>, is the life-breath;
its emission serves as the means of filling.
It constantly fills
the chest of living beings, being stationed [there].
Through exhalation, inhalation, and coughing,
<s>Prāṇa</s>, abiding with the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul),
effects departure [of the breath] —
therefore it is called <s>Prāṇa</s>.
<s>Apāna</s> carries downward
the food of men;
urine, semen, and waste — [this] wind
is therefore called <s>Apāna</s>.
What is drunk, eaten, smelled,
blood, bile, phlegm, and the like —

[this] wind is called <s>Samāna</s>.

children.translated_text: seized by a single wind, it plays with beings bewildered by births and deaths.
The <s>nāḍīcakra</s> (wheel of channels) as it truly is
I shall teach in proper sequence.
This wheel has ten spokes;
its division arises thus:
the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) revolves in the wheel
through the ten stations in sequence.
That <s>jīva</s> of the world of the living —
the deluded do not understand [it].
The <s>jīva</s> moves in ten ways;
therefore it is called a 'wheel' (<s>cakra</s>).
It is called the <s>nāḍīcakra</s> (channel-wheel)
by which it traverses.
In the space of the heart, [there is] an eight-petalled lotus, and within it the pericarp;
in the heart, upon the lotus, [there are] powers (<s>śaktis</s>) having the lustre of sun, moon, fire, and gold;

The solar is the right path, and the lunar is declared as the other;

children.translated_text: In the southern [petal], the nature of <s>Yama</s> (Death); in the southwestern, the nature of <s>Nirṛti</s> (Destruction) is indicated;
in the <s>Varuṇa</s>-petal, the nature of <s>Varuṇa</s> (Water); gone to the wind-petal, [one attains] the nature of wind.
In the northern, the nature of <s>Soma</s> (Moon); in the <s>Īśāna</s>-[petal], [the nature] is declared as that of <s>Īśāna</s>;
to whichever direction [the breath] goes, it attains that nature entirely.
Through the conjunction in the interstices of the petals, the self shines as if void;
thus indeed is the course of the individual (<s>pudgala</s>) — the principal <s>maṇḍala</s> (circle) with the <s>nāḍīs</s> (channels) as its basis.
It has been taught here for the sake of <s>siddhi</s> (attainment); it should be understood carefully as established.
Section on the <s>Nāḍīcakra</s> (Wheel of Channels) — the tenth chapter.
That <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) of the world of the living —
how is it known as the inner self (<s>adhyātma</s>)?
I have a doubt, O <s>Mahādeva</s> (Great God);
be gracious, O wielder of the trident.
Of the <s>jīva</s> known as <s>Puruṣa</s> (the Soul),
listen to the exposition, O <s>Ṣaṇmukha</s> (Six-faced One).
I shall tell [you] — there is no doubt —
especially out of affection for [my] son.
The transit (<s>saṃkrānti</s>) and the equinox (<s>viṣuva</s>),
day and night, and the solstices (<s>ayanas</s>),
the intercalary month (<s>adhimāsa</s>), the debt (<s>ṛṇa</s>),
the deficient night (<s>ūnarātra</s>), and wealth (<s>dhana</s>) —
the deficient night is to be known as sneezing;
the intercalary month is yawning;
debt is to be known as coughing;
exhalation (<s>niśvāsa</s>) is called wealth.
The northern and southern [courses] should be known
as situated in the left and right [channels];
the equinox (<s>viṣuvat</s>) is said to be in the middle,
issuing from the two cavities.
The transit (<s>saṃkrānti</s>) of this [breath] again
[is] from its own station to [another] station.
<s>Iḍā</s> and <s>Piṅgalā</s>,
and <s>Amā</s> (the new-moon channel) as the third —
<s>Suṣumnā</s> is in the middle limb;
<s>Iḍā</s> is declared in the left;
<s>Piṅgalā</s> is in the right limb;
among these, the transit (<s>saṃkrānti</s>) is spoken of.
The upward <s>prāṇa</s> is called the day;
<s>Apāna</s> is called the night.
The ten divisions of <s>prāṇa</s> —
whoever knows them thus is a knower of the <s>Veda</s>.
The extension (<s>āyāma</s>) situated in the middle of the body
is regarded as the eclipse of the moon;
that which is beyond the body, the wise one should know
as the eclipse of the sun.
Twenty-one thousand
and six hundred —
in a day and a night, the lord of <s>yogins</s>
performs that number of <s>japas</s> (repetitions).
I shall teach you <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath control)
in brief, in its entirety.
One should utter the <s>Praṇava</s> (<s>Oṃ</s>)
with a single breath, the knower of <s>yoga</s>.
Having filled the belly
with wind as much as desired,
this is the <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath control)
called <s>Pūraka</s> (the filling [of the body]).
Having closed all the gates [of the senses],
devoid of exhalation and inhalation,
one should remain like a full vessel —
that <s>prāṇāyāma</s> is <s>Kumbhaka</s> (retention).
Then one should release the wind upwards,
with a single breath, the knower of <s>yoga</s>;
conjoined with the practice of exhalation,
one should expel [the breath] as far upward [as possible].
This is known as <s>Recaka</s> (expulsion),
which brings the <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath) into peril.
That lotus which is ever in the heart,
situated facing downward —
it blossoms upward
when filled by <s>Pūraka</s> (inhalation);
the lotus becomes upward-flowing
when restrained by <s>Kumbhaka</s> (retention).
When cast by <s>Recaka</s> (exhalation),
which instantly seizes the <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath),
having released the heart-lotus
established in the upward flow,
the expelled [breath] goes upward,
having pierced the knot in an instant.
Having broken through the gate of the skull,
the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) is expelled upward.
Having gone to the station of <s>Sadāśiva</s>,
one does not again obtain birth.
The extension (<s>āyāma</s>) is performed for that [soul]
and never for another.
That <s>jīva</s> of the world of the living
has been taught by me in brief.
Thus the eleventh chapter.
Conjoined like the moon and fire,
the primordial <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s> —
she should be known in the region of the heart,
situated in the form of a sprout.
One should place the <s>sṛṣṭinyāsa</s> (creative placement) there,
uttered through double practice;
the supreme practitioner (<s>sādhaka</s>) should visualize
the nectar (<s>amṛta</s>) flowing therein.
All the world, movable and immovable,
is of the nature of fire and moon (<s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s>);
one who desires <s>siddhi</s> (attainment), being concentrated,
should contemplate the reverse.
The wise one should visualize one's own body
as having a divine, incomparable form.
Whatever ritual action is prescribed
for whoever, that action one should contemplate.
And whoever practices this
nectar (<s>amṛta</s>) facing in all directions,
within a short time
becomes a partaker of the fruit of <s>siddhi</s> (attainment).
Without knowing the <s>sṛṣṭinyāsa</s> (creative placement),
how can a practitioner (<s>sādhaka</s>) practice?
He would be striking the sky with fists —
like one pounding husks.
Thus the twelfth chapter.
Now I shall teach
the creation (<s>sṛṣṭi</s>) of the <s>mantra</s>-script in sequence —
how the <s>sakala</s> (manifest) God,
conjoined with the <s>niṣkala</s> (formless),
produced the <s>kalā</s> (creative power)
that sets all <s>mantras</s> in motion.
<s>Oṃkāra</s> is at the summit, abiding in the middle,
and <s>Oṃkāra</s> is all-pervading likewise.
The first line of <s>Oṃkāra</s>
the Lord creates.
That <s>kalā</s> (power) is called <s>Vidyā</s> (Knowledge);
it is established in every syllable.
The line that appears as having the lustre of the <s>u</s>-sound
of <s>Oṃkāra</s>,
that should be known as <s>Pratiṣṭhā</s> (Foundation).
born from the syllable 'u'.
At the crown of that [<s>Oṃkāra</s>], there exists
a subtle line, pure and stainless;
the syllable 'ma' arose there —
that <s>kalā</s> (phase of power) is called <s>Nivṛtti</s> (cessation).
Conjoined at the crown of <s>Oṃkāra</s>,
the dissolution [occurs] at the summit of <s>Oṃkāra</s>;
this line, dissolved in the void (<s>vyoman</s>) —
that <s>kalā</s> is called <s>Śānti</s> (peace).
Through conjunction it shines forth,
abiding in the <s>sakala</s> (differentiated) within the <s>niṣkala</s> (undifferentiated);
having pervaded the <s>Oṃkāra</s> at its summit,
sound (<s>śabda</s>) is born there.
That is the supreme, subtle <s>Śakti</s> (power),
regarded as conjoined with the <s>bindu</s> (point);
like a great radiance from a lamp,
accompanied by the crests of sparks.
Descending, it goes in three ways,
characterized by <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Vidyā</s>, and <s>Ātman</s>;
<s>Śānti</s> (peace), <s>Vidyā</s> (knowledge), <s>Pratiṣṭhā</s> (foundation),
and <s>Nivṛtti</s> (cessation) — these are the <s>kalās</s> (phases of power).
That <s>kalā</s> which is linear (<s>rekhinī</s>), there
having descended together with the <s>bindu</s> —
together with the Lord of <s>Vidyā</s>, <s>Śiva</s> is declared
as <s>Sadāśiva</s>, the God of Gods.
The first seed (<s>bīja</s>) of that
is called <s>Nāda</s> (resonance) and <s>Bindu</s> (point);
it does not leave the supreme abode,
which is eternal, fixed, and imperishable.
Having cast the <s>bindu</s> into its womb,
it protects it like a mother;
above it, on the left side,
the seed of <s>Viṣṇu</s> is established.
On the right, abiding in the source of <s>Brahmā</s> —
one alone, stationed in three ways;
accompanied by two <s>bindus</s> on either side,
that line is stationed in the middle.
There the subtle God <s>Śiva</s>,
the Auspicious One (<s>Śaṃkara</s>), stands concealed;
that supreme divine seed,
<s>Maheśvara</s> (the Great Lord), bearing <s>Śakti</s> in his womb.
From which all things proceed —
<s>mantras</s>, <s>tantras</s>, and the moving and unmoving [world];
unmanifest, supreme, subtle,
whose body is <s>Śakti</s>, stainless,
<s>Śiva</s>, who is without beginning or end —
knowing whom, one is not born again.
The seed stationed on the right —
that is the supreme <s>Jñānaśakti</s> (power of knowledge).
That seed is the lower <s>Brahmā</s>,
within which he abides concealed;
and the supreme <s>bindu</s> going to the left —
that is the supreme <s>Kriyāśakti</s> (power of action).
There <s>Viṣṇu</s> himself, in that seed,
abides concealed, subtle, and stainless;
this God too, stationed in creation,
was emitted by <s>Śambhu</s> (<s>Śiva</s>).
Because of being concealed, they do not see
him by whom the moving and unmoving [world] was created;
from emission (<s>visarga</s>) creation is born —
he alone is <s>Īśvara</s>, the Lord.
That seed by which [all] was emitted —
by that it is called <s>Visarga</s> (emission);
by that this [universe] is pervaded,
and the entire world consists of that.
By the assemblage of rays of <s>Śakti</s>,
by hundreds and by thousands,
this [Lord] creates and absorbs,
he who joins and separates.
By the power of knowledge (<s>Jñānaśakti</s>), the Blessed One,
<s>Śiva</s>, bestows grace;
from emission (<s>visarga</s>) comes creation,
and dissolution together with the <s>bindu</s>;
<s>Nirvāṇa</s> (liberation) is the knowledge of the <s>tattvas</s> (principles) —
within the scope of the elaboration of the <s>tantra</s>.
Section on the creation of <s>mantras</s>.
Dissolution and creation —
all has been declared, O Lord;
the fall from the path (<s>gatibhraṃśa</s>) of the initiated —
tell me about that in brief.
In [association with] a deceiver, a rogue, a cruel one,
one devoid of goodness, one fond of quarrels,
in the <s>yoga</s> that causes the fall from the path —
hear the truth of that, O <s>Ṣaṇmukha</s> (Six-faced One).
Having performed [the rite] at the crown and having projected
the moon (<s>śaśin</s>) gradually by extension,
contemplating the path as before with the mind,
one should reverse his course.
The <s>saṃhāra</s> (destruction) enclosure, the secret [formula],
at the beginning and at the end, O <s>Ṣaḍānana</s> (Six-faced One),
offering a hundred [oblations] in the <s>Mātṛkā</s> (alphabet of divine mothers),
for each one separately.
Section on the fall from the path.
Having raised the <s>nāda</s> (resonance) in the <s>prāsāda</s> (mantra-temple),
the person who recites constantly —
in six months he shall attain <s>siddhi</s> (perfection),
united in <s>yoga</s>, without doubt.
For one who recites the going and coming (<s>gamāgama</s>),
the destruction of all sins shall occur;
the lordship of the powers beginning with <s>aṇimā</s> (becoming minute) —
in six months, without doubt.
Having understood the going and coming,
one is liberated — there is no doubt in this;
having become absorbed in that, dissolved in that,
in six months one attains <s>siddhi</s> (perfection).
Gross, subtle, and supreme —
thus the <s>prāsāda</s> (mantra-temple) has been described by me;
those who do not understand the <s>prāsāda</s>
do not understand <s>Śaṅkara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>).
Section on the divisions of the <s>prāsāda</s>.
Hereafter I shall expound
the characteristics of the <s>prāsāda</s>:
short, long, and protracted (<s>pluta</s>) —
the knower of <s>mantras</s> should always observe these.
The short [form] burns away sins;
the long bestows liberation;
the protracted (<s>pluta</s>) is for nourishment (<s>āpyāyana</s>),
adorned with the <s>bindu</s> at the summit.
Three are declared as the gross divisions —
for subjugation (<s>vaśya</s>), expulsion (<s>uccāṭana</s>), and killing (<s>māraṇa</s>);
by the protracted form, subjugation (<s>vaśya</s>) is always
accomplished — there is no doubt in this.
The long form swiftly expels,
with the <s>phaṭkāra</s> (the syllable 'phaṭ') — without doubt;
at the beginning and end of the short form,
the <s>phaṭkāra</s> is prescribed for killing.
At the beginning and end, the <s>hṛdaya</s> (heart-syllable),
the <s>yoga</s> is prescribed for attraction (<s>ākarṣaṇa</s>);
the practitioner, yoked [in yoga], assuredly attracts
one stationed a hundred <s>yojanas</s> away.
Thus one should attract the target,
having truly known [their] name;
for the practitioner (<s>sādhaka</s>), [the recitation] should be abundant;
for the target (<s>sādhya</s>), it is declared to be lesser.
Having thus understood, the wise one
assuredly performs the attraction;
but without properly understanding this,
success is never achieved.
Having performed the worship (<s>yāga</s>) as previously described,
one should offer <s>arghya</s> (water offering) to the <s>mantra</s>;
having offered the <s>arghya</s> to the <s>mantra</s>,
the discerning one should perform <s>japa</s> (recitation).
On the right side of the deity,
standing, one should recite five hundred thousand [times];
at the conclusion of the <s>japa</s>, a <s>homa</s> (fire oblation) with ghee
should be [performed] ten thousand [times].
The <s>mantra</s> thus nourished
becomes fit for [ritual] action thereafter;
actions both prescribed and unspecified
attain success — without doubt.
For one who recites ten hundred thousand [times],
people dwelling in their own regions
come under his control swiftly —
such is the definitive teaching of the <s>śāstra</s>.
For one who recites fifteen hundred thousand [times],
the people dwelling in ten villages
come under his control,
with their persons and their wealth.
Thus, with twenty hundred thousand [recitations]
of the <s>prāsāda</s>, O <s>Ṣaḍānana</s>,
the <s>mantra</s>-practitioner assuredly brings under control
the lords of various regions.
With twenty-five hundred thousand [recitations],
one brings a [whole] district under control;
from thirty hundred thousand recitations,
a <s>maṇḍalin</s> (provincial governor) comes under his sway.
Reciting thirty-five hundred thousand [times],
one brings the earth under control;
from forty hundred thousand recitations, one beholds
the God <s>Hāṭakeśvara</s>.
Having recited fifty hundred thousand [times],
one becomes equal to a <s>Vidyādhara</s> (a celestial knowledge-bearer);
the <s>mantra</s>-practitioner rejoices there
until the dissolution of the elements.
Section on the characteristics of the <s>prāsāda</s> — the sixteenth chapter.
Even now, O God, doubt [remains]
clearly regarding <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge) and <s>vijñāna</s> (realization);
how indeed is knowledge known,
and how is the knowable described?
Having first understood the support (<s>ādhāra</s>),
and then the supported (<s>ādheya</s>) —
the wise one who knows support and supported
is capable in all actions.
The support is called the city (<s>pura</s>, i.e., the body);
the supported is called <s>Īśa</s> (the Lord);
the wise one who has realized <s>Īśa</s>
always rejoices of himself.
Endowed with the <s>puryaṣṭaka</s> (the eightfold subtle body),
he indeed goes downward and upward;
sound (<s>śabda</s>), touch (<s>sparśa</s>), form (<s>rūpa</s>),
taste (<s>rasa</s>), and smell (<s>gandha</s>) — these five,
intellect (<s>buddhi</s>), mind (<s>manas</s>), and ego (<s>ahaṅkāra</s>) —
these are declared as the <s>puryaṣṭaka</s> (eightfold subtle body);

children.text: Note that this definition of the puryaṣṭaka is not
accepted by Ram without considerable distortion.

children.translated_text: as long as one is not freed from these,
how can one be released from bondage?
In <s>Brahmā</s>, one should abandon touch and sound;
in <s>Keśava</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), one should abandon taste;
in <s>Rudra</s>, one should abandon form and smell;
in <s>Īśvara</s>, intellect and ego;
having abandoned mind and <s>bindu</s> in <s>Śiva</s>,
freed from these, one goes to <s>Śiva</s>.
Section on <s>Vijñāna</s> (Realization) — the seventeenth chapter.
The procedure of the <s>Kālacakra</s> (Wheel of Time),
I shall now expound in due order;
it is known as the <s>Kālacakra</s>,
by which time is awakened.
When the breath traverses in three days and nights [cycles],
he lives for three years;
when the breath traverses in two days and nights [cycles],
he lives for two years.
When the breath traverses in [the cycle of] one day and night,
he lives for one year;
when it goes [only during] one day
and one night likewise —
death arises in six months —
such is the definitive teaching of the <s>śāstra</s>;
through the passage of the second [breath],
he lives for [only] a day and night.
As the first (<s>ādyā</s>), so the left (<s>vāmā</s>),
and the middle (<s>madhyamā</s>) likewise;
thus the <s>Kālacakra</s> (Wheel of Time) has been declared,
out of special affection as to a son.
Section on the <s>Kālacakra</s> — the eighteenth chapter.
Previously it was stated thus:
'The division of <s>Śiva</s> is eightfold' —
how is it differentiated, O Lord of the Gods?
Tell me the truth, O Lord.
<s>Sakala</s> (with parts), <s>Niṣkala</s> (without parts), <s>Śūnya</s> (void),
<s>Kalāḍhya</s> (rich in <s>kalā</s>), <s>Khamalaṅkṛta</s> (adorned with space),
<s>Kṣapaṇa</s> (consuming), <s>Antastha</s> (indwelling),
and <s>Kaṇṭhoṣṭhya</s> (gutturo-labial) — the eighth, they know.

children.text: This verse is NisMula 6:6 (f.21verso, line 2) [reading smṛtam for viduḥ]

children.translated_text: The <s>prāsāda</s> conjoined with the sixth [vowel],
accompanied by the six-ending [consonant] —
<s>Sakala</s>, abiding in all beings,
is proclaimed as the <s>Śiva-tattva</s> (principle of Śiva).
The God himself departs,
having abandoned the body, ascending upward;
one should know that <s>Niṣkala</s> [form of] <s>Śiva</s>
as devoid of the six syllables.
Having abandoned inhalation and exhalation,
remaining in the body like a log of wood —
one should know that as <s>Śūnya</s> (void),
and should contemplate it in the heart.
With the mouth in the form of a kiss —
that principle (<s>tattva</s>) has been proclaimed;
one should know that as <s>Kalāḍhya</s> (rich in <s>kalā</s>);
now hear about the one stationed in space (<s>ākāśa</s>).

children.text: aiśa treatment of ṛ in śṛṇu [making the previous syllable long]

children.translated_text: When the upward <s>nāda</s> (resonance) has diminished,
that which is proclaimed as its end —
one should know [<s>Śiva</s>] stationed there
as adorned with space (<s>ākāśa</s>).
With the mouth held open —
thus one should utter [the name of] the World-Teacher (<s>Jagadguru</s>);
'destroying sorrow' — thus it is called;
from the destruction of that [sorrow], it is called <s>Kṣapaṇa</s> (consuming).
When the downward <s>nāda</s> has diminished,
that which is proclaimed as its end —
one should know that as <s>Antastha</s> (indwelling),
declared as unutterable.
The eighth of the seventh group (<s>varga</s>) is the vertex;
the second of the seventh [group],
transcending the groups, having six endings,
the third-fourth of the seventh —
the first should be joined again,
and the sixth of the first [group] indeed;
conjoined with a space-crowned [element] —
<s>Kaṇṭhoṣṭhya</s> (gutturo-labial) is regarded as the eighth.
These divisions have been declared
for the accomplishment of powers beginning with <s>aṇimā</s> (becoming minute);
the unutterable, without doubt,
is called <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation).
Section on the exposition of the eightfold divisions of <s>Śiva</s> — the nineteenth chapter.
How is [<s>Śiva</s>] all-pervasive — below, above,
and how does he extend in all directions?
Tell me this in truth,
out of compassion, O <s>Maheśvara</s> (Great Lord).
As long as the living being remains in a body,
so long he is established below;
having departed, he pervades in all directions;
being indwelling, he is stationed everywhere.
The God, established in the three paths,
abides in all bodies;
without knowing [this], one is not liberated,
even if one attains dissolution.
That threefold path, [with] three supports,
abides in all bodies;
whoever knows this pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>) thus —
he is all-pervading, without doubt.
For him there is no birth from a womb,
as the God declares;
one wanders in <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) for so long
as one does not find this pervasion.
Having known the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) as all-pervading,
one is liberated — there is no doubt in this;
just as an inchworm (<s>tṛṇajalūkā</s>),
when it has reached the tip of a blade of grass,
above [it is] unsupported —
likewise the <s>jīva</s> (soul) is situated here;
void above, void below,
and void stationed within the body —
whoever knows the threefold void —
he is assuredly liberated, O <s>Guha</s> (<s>Skanda</s>);
this pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>) has been declared by me
in brief, not in detail;
there is nothing higher than this,
nothing more pervasive than the all-pervading.
Section on Pervasion (<s>Vyāpti</s>) — the twentieth chapter.
Hereafter I shall expound
the eightfold proof (<s>pratyaya</s>), namely:
kindling fire without [external] fire,
and likewise the touching of a tree [to cause its death],
the paralysis (<s>stobhana</s>) of snares,
the destruction of great sins,
the neutralization of poison,
and likewise rendering [something] seedless,
and the destruction of [afflictions by] planets and fevers —
these are declared as the eightfold proof (<s>pratyaya</s>);
having thus understood [them] according to the prescribed method,
fame arises everywhere.
With <s>Praṇava</s> (<s>Oṃ</s>), stationed in the midst of fire,
the syllable 'ha' and <s>hrīṃ</s> likewise,
<s>Oṃ</s> at the beginning and <s>namaḥ</s> at the end —
this is beneficial for kindling fire without [external] fire.
Having conjoined the fire with the stream [of breath],
together with a thousand strikes (<s>udghāta</s>),
with the application of the five-syllable [<s>mantra</s>],
it blazes forth indeed — without doubt.
<s>Oṃkāra</s> below everything,
the syllable 'ra' (<s>repha</s>) stationed above it,
conjoined as before —
this application is rare on earth.
With seven hundred strikes,
a tree, when touched, dies;
and again, the reviving of that [tree]
is situated in the water stream (<s>vāruṇa srotas</s>).
That tree lives again,
just as it was before;
and again it is the same [formula],
but without the syllable 'ra' (<s>repha</s>).
In the procedure of reviving,
this [formula] is illuminated by the <s>bindu</s> in five ways,
conjoined with [the syllable] 'au' in the middle,
illuminated by <s>Praṇava</s> (<s>Oṃ</s>) at the end.
Beginning with the syllable 'ī', with 'hau' in the middle,
then with fire in the middle —
the application at the time of equinox (<s>viṣuvat</s>)
is the paralyzer of snares.
With five hundred strikes,
[the target] falls indeed — without doubt;
and again, the reviving of that one —
hear how that occurs.
Conjoined with [the syllable] 'ī' at beginning and end,
with 'hau' employed in the middle,
ignited by <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>anusvāra</s>
<s>namaḥ</s> at the end, then <s>praṇava</s> (Oṃ) again.
One should employ [this mantra] in raising up [the vital breath]
in all beings — one who knows the <s>tattvas</s> (principles).
With as many <s>udghātas</s> (upward strikes of breath)
one should apply [this] with effort.
The <s>la</s>-seed (<s>bīja</s>), combined with the <s>jīva</s> (life-breath),
situated at the beginning and end of the <s>ha</s>-syllable,
and placed in the middle as before,
accompanied by <s>vāyu</s> (wind) and <s>bindu</s> (dot) —
What was taught regarding the ascent [of breath],
whereby heaviness arises —
I shall teach again
how lightness arises.
<s>Oṃkāra</s> (the syllable Oṃ), <s>haṃ</s>, with <s>ya</s>-syllable,
and <s>au</s>-syllable, <s>haṃ</s>, <s>namaḥ</s> likewise —
this is the <s>tulāpuruṣayoga</s> (the practice of balancing the person),
with ten thousand <s>udghātas</s> (breath-strikes).
That <s>ha</s>-syllable, kindled by <s>va</s>-syllable
and <s>ya</s>-syllable,
<s>hyau</s> in the middle, <s>hlīṃ namaḥ</s> at the end —
the wise one [uses this] with the <s>Vāruṇa</s> (water-path) method.
With eight hundred <s>udghātas</s> (breath-strikes)
one certainly draws out poison.
Just as is seen in igniting fire,
so too in rendering [something] seedless.
With five hundred <s>udghātas</s> (breath-strikes)
the special [practice] is prescribed here.
Making <s>Oṃkāra</s> (the syllable Oṃ) at the beginning,
then <s>hrūṃkāra</s> thereafter,
<s>hrauṃ hrūṃ</s> and <s>phaṇṇamaḥ</s> at the end —
this is regarded [as the mantra] for the destruction of <s>grahas</s> (seizing spirits).
In the application through the <s>Vāruṇa</s> (water) path,
with eight hundred <s>udghātas</s> (breath-strikes),
beginning with <s>praṇava</s> (Oṃ), then <s>huṃ phaṭ</s>,

children.text: huṃ phaṭ huṃ phaṭ tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: <s>huṃ phaṭ</s>, <s>huṃ phaṭ</s>, and likewise

children.text: phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ phaḍevaṃ syād
children.translated_text: <s>phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ</s> — thus it should be.
The wise one, through the <s>Vāruṇa</s> (water) method,
with eight hundred <s>udghātas</s> (breath-strikes),
swiftly destroys fever.
Thus ends the twenty-first chapter, the section on <s>pratyaya</s> (conviction/application).
What kind of <s>prāsāda</s> (cosmic temple) is to be known?
And what is its pervasion?
What is its body like?
Tell [me], O <s>Maheśvara</s> (Great Lord)!
He who does not know the <s>prāsāda</s> (cosmic temple)
as the great body of the five <s>mantras</s> (<s>pañcamantra</s>),
endowed with thirty-eight <s>kalās</s> (parts) —
he is not called an <s>ācārya</s> (preceptor).
Without properly knowing the <s>prāsāda</s> (cosmic temple),
the <s>guru</s> (teacher) who performs <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation)
leads his disciple and himself
downward — of this there is no doubt.
But he who performs <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation)
standing within the lotus-crest of the <s>prāsāda</s> (cosmic temple),
that <s>ācārya</s> (preceptor), together with his disciple,
attains union with <s>Śiva</s> (<s>śivasāyujya</s>).
<s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Rudra</s>,
<s>Indra</s>, <s>Candra</s> (the Moon), <s>Bṛhaspati</s>,
<s>Prajāpati</s> and likewise <s>Āditya</s> (the Sun),
<s>Śukra</s>, <s>Skanda</s>, and <s>Bhṛgu</s> likewise —
these and other living divine beings
are all declared to be born of the <s>prāsāda</s> (cosmic temple).
These and many other
<s>munis</s> (sages) of firm vows
meditate upon the supreme <s>Haṃsa</s> (Swan),
the <s>prāsāda</s> (cosmic temple) in name and form.
I shall describe its divisions,
by meditating upon which one partakes of immortality.
<s>Sadyojāta</s>, joined with eight <s>kalās</s> (parts),
is known to be born of the syllable <s>a</s>.
<s>Vāmadeva</s> is born of the syllable <s>u</s>, from <s>Vidyā</s> (knowledge);
<s>Aghora</s> is born of the syllable <s>ma</s>.
<s>Puruṣa</s> (Tatpuruṣa) should be known as born of <s>bindu</s> (the dot);
<s>Īśāna</s> is born of the crest (<s>śikhā</s>).
Thus these five <s>mantras</s>
arise from the <s>prāsāda</s> (cosmic temple).
Ten billion
<s>mantras</s> of immeasurable power —
through the grace of the desired [deity],
all desires are fulfilled — of this there is no doubt.
The nine <s>Mārutas</s> (wind-deities) beginning with <s>Śakti</s>,
and whatever <s>mantras</s> have been proclaimed —
all are born from the lotus of the <s>prāsāda</s> (cosmic temple)
and are all of unfailing power.
<s>Sadyojāta</s> should be known as earth;
<s>Vāmadeva</s> is declared to be water;
<s>Aghora</s> is called fire;
<s>Tatpuruṣa</s> is said to be wind.
<s>Īśāna</s> is space (<s>ākāśa</s>),
the self-existent God, <s>Maheśvara</s> (the Great Lord).
<s>Sadyojāta</s> is the <s>Ṛgveda</s>;
<s>Vāmadeva</s> is said to be the <s>Yajurveda</s>.
<s>Aghora</s> is the <s>Sāmaveda</s>;
<s>Tatpuruṣa</s> is said to be the <s>Atharvaveda</s>.
The fifth is the supreme, subtle [Veda],
pervading space — <s>Sadāśiva</s>.
<s>Sadyojāta</s> is indeed <s>Brahmā</s>;
<s>Vāmadeva</s> is declared to be <s>Viṣṇu</s>;
<s>Aghora</s> has <s>Rudra</s> as its deity;
<s>Tatpuruṣa</s> is said to be <s>Īśvara</s>.
<s>Īśāna</s> has <s>Śiva</s> as its deity,
stationed in the heart and so forth.
But the sixth supreme <s>tattva</s> (principle)
abides with qualities of incomparability.
Its body is not to be described
by qualities born of <s>Prakṛti</s> (material nature).
Having known the supreme ladder
that proceeds through the five stations,
what has once been known by someone —
that expanded [knowledge] is itself that [supreme reality].
At that very moment he is liberated,
when that state (<s>pada</s>) is known.
Thus ends the twenty-second chapter, the section on the determination of the <s>prāsāda</s> (cosmic temple).
Listen, O <s>Ṣaṇmukha</s> (Six-faced One),
to the supreme <s>jñānāmṛta</s> (nectar of knowledge), in truth,
which has not been told to anyone —
I shall speak that which is not to be spoken.
The <s>sakala</s> (with parts) should be known as dwelling in the body;
the <s>niṣkala</s> (without parts) is devoid of body.
He is accessible through the instruction of the qualified (<s>āpta</s>),
abiding everywhere as something [indefinable].
He who says '<s>haṃsa</s>, <s>haṃsa</s>' —
that <s>Haṃsa</s> is the God <s>Sadāśiva</s>.
He is obtained from the mouth of the <s>guru</s> (teacher),
directly perceivable, facing all directions.
Just as oil [resides] in sesame seeds,
just as fragrance abides in a flower,
so <s>Puruṣa</s> (the Supreme Person) abides in this body,
both outside and within.
Just as someone holding a torch,
having seen the object, discards the torch —
having seen the knowable through knowledge,
so one should abandon [even] knowledge.
The flower should be known as <s>sakala</s> (with parts);
its fragrance is <s>niṣkala</s> (without parts).
The tree should be known as <s>sakala</s> (with parts);
its shadow is <s>niṣkala</s> (without parts).
The <s>niṣkala</s> (partless) state
is established everywhere within the <s>sakala</s> (with parts).
The means (<s>upāya</s>) is <s>sakala</s> (with parts);
the goal (<s>upeya</s>) is <s>niṣkala</s> (without parts).
In the <s>sakala</s> (with parts), the disposition is <s>sakala</s>;
in the <s>niṣkala</s> (without parts), it is <s>niṣkala</s> likewise.
Three <s>mātrās</s> (measures), two <s>mātrās</s>,
and one <s>mātrā</s> likewise —
the half <s>mātrā</s> is supreme and subtle;
beyond it is the supreme beyond the supreme.
<s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Rudra</s>,
<s>Īśvara</s>, and <s>Śiva</s> himself —
in fivefold form, with five deities,
the <s>sakala</s> (with parts) is recited.
The station of <s>Brahmā</s> is the heart;
<s>Viṣṇu</s> is situated in the throat.
<s>Rudra</s> is situated in the middle of the palate;
<s>Maheśvara</s> (the Great Lord) is at the forehead.
One should know <s>Śiva</s> at the tip of the nose;
beyond that is the supreme state (<s>paraṃ padam</s>).
Beyond the supreme there is nothing —
this is the certain conclusion of the <s>śāstra</s> (scripture).
How is there coming and going for him?
And by whom is he led?
I have a doubt, O <s>Mahādeva</s> (Great God);
tell [me] as it truly is.
By <s>Śakti</s> (power) the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) is led;
having reached that [state], it returns.
I shall tell you its end;
listen, O <s>Ṣaṇmukha</s> (Six-faced One), to the truth.
One should know that which transcends the body
as [being] twelve finger-breadths above the tip of the nose.
One should know its end [to be] there;
stationed there, the Lord pervades [all].
Even if the mind is cast elsewhere,
even if the eyes are directed elsewhere,
even so, the <s>yoga</s> (union) of <s>yogins</s>
continues uninterrupted.
This is that supreme secret;
this is that supreme imperishable [syllable].
There is nothing higher than this;
there is no <s>Śiva</s> higher than this;
there is no knowledge higher than this —
thus speaks the Blessed Lord <s>Śiva</s>.
Having obtained the nectar of <s>Śiva</s>-knowledge
in brief, not in detail —
the determination of the supreme imperishable [syllable]
has been spoken by the God of gods.
This is the true being of <s>Śiva</s> for you,
issued forth from the mouth of <s>Śiva</s>,
the most secret of secrets, hidden —
to be concealed with effort.
It should not be given to one who is not a disciple,
nor to one who is not a [worthy] son, ever.
To one devoted to the <s>guru</s>, the gods, and the sacred fire,
and to one constantly devoted to liberation —
this <s>śāstra</s> (scripture) should be given;
it should not be given to others.
The giver [to unworthy recipients] goes to hell
and never attains <s>siddhi</s> (perfection).
The nectar of <s>Śiva</s> has been proclaimed by me;
this is true, true for you.
Having known this, the wise one
should live freely as he pleases.
Whether a householder or a celibate student,
a forest-dweller or a mendicant —
wherever the knower abides,
always knowing the supreme imperishable [syllable],
even one attached to sense objects
attains <s>Śiva</s> at the end of the body.
From the knowledge of this <s>śāstra</s> (scripture) alone,
a person in any condition whatsoever
is not stained by merit or sin
such as the killing of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> or [the merit of] a horse sacrifice.
The impeller (<s>codaka</s>), the awakener (<s>bodhaka</s>),
and the bestower of liberation (<s>mokṣada</s>) — he is regarded as the highest.
Thus the <s>ācārya</s> (preceptor) should be known
as threefold on this earth.
The impeller shows the path;
the awakener points out the station;
the bestower of liberation [reveals] the supreme <s>tattva</s> (principle),
knowing which, one partakes of immortality.
Thus ends the twenty-third chapter, the section on the nectar of knowledge (<s>jñānāmṛta</s>).
